findings.problem: The whole direction rests on one sentence: editing is moving something nearer. That move is also the only animated thing in the entire product (one 0.22s transition on top, b.css:136). Driven at 390x844 the edited item opens at top:996 in an 844-tall viewport; at 768x1024 it opens at top:1056; at 1024x900 at top:1016. In all three the item is below the fold, nothing scrolls it into view, and the bottom sheet then occupies the lower 380-400px of the screen. So on a phone and on a tablet the owner presses +7, the count updates, the date line updates, the readout updates, focus survives, the page keeps its place - every assertion the gate makes is true - and the person sees nothing move. The single designed moment of feeling in this product is unreachable on the device the owner is most likely holding. Above 1280 it works and it is lovely, which is what makes the loss legible. It is not a layout impossibility: scrolling the item manually to top:200 at 390 and pressing +7 moves it to top:326, fully visible above the sheet at 464.
findings.fix: In render-b.js, on opening the editor and on every stepper press below 1280, scroll the edited item into the strip between the page top and the sheet's top edge. Concretely: after paint, measure the sheet's getBoundingClientRect().top (or the viewport height when the editor is the static left rail at 1280+), define visibleBottom = sheetTop - 24, and if the item's rect falls outside the band [72, visibleBottom - itemHeight] scroll the window by the difference over the declared 0.22s ease so the scroll and the item's own top transition read as one gesture. Run it before the transition starts on open, and after each move only when the item has left that band, so a move that stays visible never scrolls the page under the thumb.

findings.problem: This product's argument is that the count is the whole composition - the type ramp reserves 96 and 148 for one thing only, and every approach screen honours it: 148px at 1440, 96px on a phone. On the wedding morning, the one screen with the most feeling in the brief, the largest element on the page is Mara & Finn at 48px, the count resolves to the word Today set at 12px in mono, and Wedding day - the event itself, on the day itself - is set at 24px. Measured across states: owner-flight 148, desk 148, phone 96, day 48. The composition builds for 79 days and then, on arrival, deflates to a third of its scale and whispers. A guest opening this on the morning gets a smaller, more tentative screen than the one they got in July. That is emotionally backwards, and it is the difference between a product that functions and one that gives you a lump in the throat.
findings.fix: In render-b.js and b.css, give the day state the count slot at full scale: set the word Today in Geist 600 at the 96 step on phone and the 148 step at desk width, in the exact position the number occupies on every other state (above the date line, with the mono micro-label beneath it reading the weekday rather than DAYS). Demote Mara & Finn to the 20 step above it, where MARA & FINN already sits on every other surface, so the day screen is recognisably the same composition arriving rather than a different card. Keep Happening now / Wedding day where it is but lift Wedding day to the 30 step. No new tokens: 96, 148, 30 and 20 are already in the ramp.

findings.element: state=publish, .b-barActs buttons Send the link and Copy the link
findings.problem: The brief names this state as the ceremony - handing someone a finished print - and it is the moment the owner has been working toward. What is built is a heading, a paragraph, a URL in a box and two buttons, over roughly 55% dead page below 960px. Driven, both are real button elements and both do nothing: pressing Send the link leaves the DOM byte-identical, pressing Copy the link leaves the DOM byte-identical, no acknowledgement, no copied state, no clipboard write. The gate's dead-control assertion runs only on owner-flight and owner-empty and only inside .b-field, so these two escape it. The lock's own rule is that anything not built has no button element. The result is that the emotional peak of the owner's journey is the one place the product goes silent when you press it, while the unfurl card - the best object in the whole lab - sits inert in a left column as a caption.
findings.fix: Make Copy the link real: navigator.clipboard.writeText on the token URL, swap the label to Copied, announce it through the existing role=status live region, revert the label after 2s. Make Send the link real by opening the platform share sheet where navigator.share exists and otherwise a mailto: with subject 'Mara and Finn, a wedding timeline' and the URL as the body - or, if neither is in scope for the lab, delete both button elements and leave the URL field with one working Copy control, per the lock's own rule. Separately, promote the unfurl card into the right-hand column at the same width as the message block, so what the owner is looking at while they press Copy is the thing that lands in the message.

findings.problem: Driven at 1440: with 7 moments on the measure, pressing Delete this moment removes one, and the reversibility surface stays data-empty=true with its Undo control still disabled. Ctrl+Z does nothing; the count stays at 6. So a one-day nudge is undoable and permanently destroying a moment from someone's wedding plan is not, with no confirmation either. The gate proves delete removes the moment and the measure reflows; it never asks whether you can get it back. Emotionally this is the opposite of what the surface promises everywhere else - the whole register is that this is being held safely for you - and it is the one place a planner acting fast at 11pm loses real work. Delete also sits immediately beside Done at near-equal weight, one target away from the safe action.
findings.fix: Route delete through the same history stack the steppers use in render-b.js: push the removed item and its index before splicing, set the undo bar text to 'Last change: Send the invitations deleted.' and enable its control, and have undo() reinsert the item at its original index and return focus to that row. No confirmation dialog is then needed. Separately, drop Delete this moment out of the Done row onto its own line beneath the sheet's bottom rule, at the 13 step and the 0.62 alpha, so it stops competing with the safe action.

findings.problem: The reversibility surface is honest, singular, live and it names its key - and it is rendered at the very bottom of the document. Measured after pressing Move a week later with no scrolling: at 1440x960 it lands at top:1911 in a 960 viewport; at 390x844 it lands at top:2263 in an 844 viewport. inView is false in both. The reassurance is announced roughly 1000 to 1400 pixels below where the person's eyes and thumb are, at the exact instant they most need it. The lessons library asks for one reversibility surface with a place it lives; this has a place, and the place is off-screen. The felt consequence is that changing a date has no aftermath - the moment slides, and then nothing tells you you are safe, so the fifteen seconds this round was meant to fix still end in silence.
findings.fix: Anchor .b-undo to the edge the editor lives on so it is on screen by construction whenever it has something to say: at 1280 and up, pin it inside the left rail directly beneath the editor plate (position: sticky; bottom: 24px within the rail); below 1280, make it the top strip of the same fixed sheet, above WHAT IT IS. Keep it collapsed to zero height and silent while data-empty=true so it reserves nothing at rest, and give it the 0.14s opacity transition already in the motion set on appear. Not a floating toast - it stays one element in one place.

biggestWin: The unfurl card is the memorable moment, and it is the only one. 79 set large on ink, DAYS TO SATURDAY 3 OCTOBER 2026 in mono beneath it, arriving in a chat bubble under the line 'Here is everything, love. It updates itself.' That single object compresses the whole product - the day, the distance, the fact that it stays true without anyone maintaining it - into something a person receives rather than operates, and it is the one frame in this lab a discerning stranger would screenshot and want. Everything upstream of it is credible rather than moving: the empty state asks one question and only one, the ended link is the most gracious revocation screen I have read, the loading frame invents nothing, and the print keepsake is a genuinely good poster. But the honest answer to this seat's question is that the received surfaces have no moment at all - phone and desk carry zero focusable elements and zero motion, so the audience gets a beautiful static poster and nothing that happens - and the one designed moment that does exist, an item sliding up the measure, is invisible at every width below 1280 and is only ever seen by the owner, who already knew the plan. The gap to 9.5 is not polish and it is not a different decision; the direction is right and the craft under it is real. It is about three builds: put the move on screen where it happens, give the day the count it earned, and make publishing something that answers you back.
